explain.say: Here is a tricky question: can a sea be a lake? Yes! Look at the two water giants on the board. Both are lakes, which means water with land all the way around it.

faq.q: What is the biggest lake in the world?
faq.a: The Caspian Sea, about 371,000 square kilometres, between Europe and Asia. For fresh water lakes, Lake Superior in North America is the biggest by area.
Lake Baikal in Siberia, Russia, about 1,642 metres deep at its deepest point.

faq.q: Why is the Caspian Sea called a sea?
faq.a: Its water is salty and it is so huge that people long ago thought of it as a sea. But it has land all around it, so geographers call it a lake.
asks: Is the Caspian Sea a lake?

faq.q: How much fresh water is in Lake Baikal?
faq.a: About one fifth of all the unfrozen fresh water on Earth's surface, more than all of North America's Great Lakes together.
asks: Does Baikal have the most fresh water?

faq.a: The nerpa, or Baikal seal, lives only in Lake Baikal. It is one of the only seals in the world that lives in fresh water.
asks: Are there seals in Lake Baikal?

facts: The Caspian Sea is the world's largest lake by area, about 371,000 square kilometres.
Lake Baikal is the deepest lake, about 1,642 metres, and holds about 20 percent of the world's unfrozen surface fresh water.
